claims.text: Coupling mechanical alloying with controlled spark plasma sintering can concurrently improve strength and ductility in equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloys relative to conventional as-cast processing.
Equiatomic NbMoTaWVTi or NbMoCrTiAl powders can be prepared from elemental constituents by mechanical alloying.
Mechanical alloying under argon followed by short-hold SPS at temperatures in the 1200–1400 °C range and applied pressure is a processing route used for equiatomic refractory HEAs.
Precise control of milling time, ball-to-powder ratio, SPS temperature, pressure, and dwell time ensures a fine microstructure and controlled precipitation.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS produces a fine-grained BCC matrix.
The processed BCC matrix contains uniformly distributed nanoscale secondary precipitates such as TiO or Laves-phase particles.
The secondary precipitates impede dislocation motion.
The precipitate-containing microstructure preserves continuous ductile matrix paths.
Mechanical alloying refines the grain structure.
Mechanical alloying initiates chemical homogenization.
Controlled SPS consolidates the mechanically alloyed powder while limiting microstructural coarsening.
Controlled SPS promotes controlled precipitation of secondary phases.
Grain-boundary strengthening increases yield strength in the processed alloy.
Precipitation strengthening increases yield strength in the processed alloy.
Maintaining sufficient ductile-matrix connectivity improves overall ductility.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS should produce a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to casting or processing without pre-alloying.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS should produce a statistically significant increase in fracture strain relative to casting or processing without pre-alloying.
Conventional as-cast or arc-melted refractory HEAs typically exhibit a strength–ductility tradeoff because of coarse microstructures or uncontrolled secondary-phase distributions.
Excessive secondary-phase precipitation or over-sintering can cause brittleness.
The effectiveness of the processing route depends on alloy composition and specific milling and sintering parameters.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a statistically significant increase in fracture strain, whereas the parenthetical falsification criterion treats unchanged fracture strain ('without a concurrent reduction') as sufficient for concurrent improvement.
